nodes.name: SynSense Speck
nodes.summary: Fully asynchronous, clockless SoC integrating a 128x128 on-chip Dynamic Vision Sensor with the DYNAP-CNN convolutional neuromorphic processor (9 fixed conv->IF->pool cores, up to ~328K neurons). Measured sub-4-microsecond end-to-end 9-layer propagation latency, with reset-by-subtraction as the documented hardware default.

attributes.time_model: Fully asynchronous, no global or local clock for the compute pipeline; computation triggered directly by event arrival (request/acknowledge circuit blocks). Speck2e+ has an optional slow clock for leak/DVS-filter/readout-averaging only, not the conv/IF compute path.
attributes.neuron_models: Nonleaky Integrate-and-Fire (IAFSqueeze) by default; optional leak requires a bias term plus slow-clock configuration.
attributes.reset_semantics: Native, hardware-configurable reset-by-subtraction is the documented default (return_to_zero=False); hard reset available via return_to_zero=True.
attributes.payload: Binary AER spike events with layer/x/y/feature/timestamp fields (microsecond resolution).
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit fixed point.
attributes.on_chip_learning: unknown (Speck line has no documented on-chip learning path; contrast SynSense's earlier DYNAP-SE analog line)
attributes.operator_coverage: 9 configurable cores, each conv(kernel up to 16x16, stride {1,2,4,8}, padding 0-7)->IF->optional sum-pooling only (AvgPool2d auto-rewritten to SumPool2d); Linear auto-converted to 1x1 Conv2d; no native BatchNorm; uniform per-layer threshold only (no per-neuron thresholds); fan-out of 2 destination cores per core.
attributes.host_interface: SPI/serial I/O, interrupt pins for up to 15+1 classes; USB 3.1 host connection for the Dev Kit.
attributes.toolchain: Sinabs (from_model/DynapcnnNetwork) -> samna runtime.
attributes.availability: Speck Dev Kit and Demo Kit are purchasable/orderable hardware products, no research-membership gate (unlike Loihi/INRC).

nodes.name: Spike-time gradient methods (SLAYER / EXODUS / EventProp)
nodes.summary: Exact or near-exact gradient methods defined directly on spike timing rather than a surrogate derivative substituted into ordinary BPTT. The one direct-training lineage with a consistently exercised, vendor-maintained silicon path: SLAYER/Lava-DL to Loihi, and EventProp/mlGeNN to Loihi 2.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Yes, routinely, via first-party vendor toolchains. SLAYER-trained CNN deployed via NxTF/NxSDK to physical Loihi 1 (DVS Gesture: latency and energy measured via a built-in performance probe). Lava-DL (SLAYER to NetX) PilotNet SDNN/LIF regression on physical Loihi 2: throughput 16.87-408.91 fps, full power/execution/memory/activity profiling. EventProp (exact-gradient BPTT) via mlGeNN to NetX to physical single-chip Loihi 2 with learned synaptic delays, on Spiking Heidelberg/Speech-Commands keyword spotting: 1.46-1.54 ms latency, 0.21-0.46 mJ energy, 18x faster and 250x less energy than an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano at batch=1. EXODUS itself (the training-speed algorithm underlying this lineage) has not been run on hardware in its own paper; deployment is exercised only downstream, via Sinabs to DynapCNN/Speck users.

nodes.name: SpiNNaker 1
nodes.summary: Manycore ARM968-based digital neuromorphic manycore system (18 cores/chip, GALS architecture, up to ~1.04M cores at full 10-cabinet scale) that simulates arbitrary software-defined neuron models at a default 1 ms real-time timestep, communicating via best-effort (drop-possible) AER packets over a custom asynchronous router fabric.

attributes.time_model: Discrete timer-interrupt timestep, default 1 ms (biologically real-time convention, not a hardware floor); sub-millisecond timesteps possible at proportional real-time-factor cost.
attributes.neuron_models: Fully software-defined via C code (sPyNNaker neural_modelling library): current/conductance-based LIF, Izhikevich, plus plugin models.
attributes.reset_semantics: Not hard-wired; achievable as either hard or soft reset via a user-definable neuron_model_has_spiked() callback, but not a sPyNNaker built-in default (built-in cell types like IF_curr_exp use PyNN-conventional hard-reset LIF/IF).
attributes.payload: Binary AER spike packets (40- or 72-bit) carrying source-neuron ID; no guaranteed delivery (packets can be re-routed late or dropped under congestion).
attributes.weight_precision: Fixed-point only (no FPU on ARM968); Q-format fixed point commonly used (e.g., Q6.16 in one deep-belief-network implementation).
attributes.on_chip_learning: STDP and structural plasticity supported in sPyNNaker's neuron/synapse model library.
attributes.operator_coverage: General-purpose PyNN neuron/synapse simulator, not a native CNN-layer framework; convolutional structure must be expressed as ordinary projections (e.g., via SNN Toolbox's build_convolution).
attributes.toolchain: sPyNNaker (PyNN backend) + SpiNNTools (partition/place/route/load/execute/extract pipeline).
attributes.availability: Hosted at University of Manchester (up to ~1.04M-core machine) plus standalone 4-/48-chip boards; free EBRAINS-account access for evaluation/basic research.
attributes.price: Not sold as a product; free access via EBRAINS Collaboratory account for research.

locators: Materials and Methods (NEST HPC cluster specification)

nodes.name: SpiNNaker 2
nodes.summary: Successor chip (22 nm FDSOI, ARM Cortex-M4F cores with FPU, 144 PEs/chip) adding a 16x4 INT8 MAC accelerator per processing element for hybrid dense-ANN/spiking execution; commercialized by SpiNNcloud Systems and deployed at multi-billion-neuron scale (Dresden, Sandia, Leipzig).

attributes.time_model: Same SpiNNaker-style discrete-timestep, software-programmable model as SpiNNaker 1, extended with fine-grained per-PE DVFS/adaptive body biasing.
attributes.neuron_models: Software-defined on Cortex-M4F cores (LIF/CuBa-LIF standard); py-spinnaker2's NIR importer supports Conv1d, Conv2d, Flatten, Affine, Linear, CuBaLIF, IF, LIF, SumPool2d.
attributes.reset_semantics: py-spinnaker2 backend supports BOTH reset-by-subtraction and reset-to-zero for IF/LIF/CuBa-LIF -- a hardware/software capability broader than what the formal NIR primitive spec itself exposes.
attributes.payload: Supports large (128-bit) packet payloads; EventProp backward-pass demo transmits signed floating-point error-gradient values as packet payloads, distinct from ordinary binary forward spikes.
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit signed synapse weights (py-spinnaker2 deployed configuration); MAC accelerator supports 8/16-bit MAC with 8/16/32-bit output.
attributes.state_precision: 32-bit floating-point neuron state/parameters (mixed precision: quantized weights, float32 dynamics).
attributes.operator_coverage: Hybrid SNN/DNN execution: same PE runs event-driven spiking code and, via the MAC array, dense 8/16-bit convolution/matmul for conventional DNN layers.
attributes.toolchain: py-spinnaker2 (PyNN-inspired API), NIR importer, Brian2-based software-emulation fallback.
attributes.availability: Commercially deployed via SpiNNcloud Systems (Dresden half-scale system, Sandia National Labs, University of Leipzig); largest system stood up ~30,000 chips as of mid-2025 (vendor statement).
attributes.price: Sold as commercial supercomputing systems/racks; per-chip/per-board pricing not published.

nodes.name: SpiNNaker runtime
nodes.summary: The on-chip SpiN1API event-driven operating system plus the host-side SpiNNTools data-loading/execution/extraction pipeline that actually runs a placed-and-routed machine graph on physical SpiNNaker silicon: per-core neuron/synapse parameter blocks and synaptic-matrix data are generated on the host and loaded into each core's ITCM/DTCM/SDRAM, all cores are signaled to start together, SpiN1API then runs the compiled C executable on each core for the configured duration, and results are read back off-machine via the PyNN API. For SpiNNaker 2, the analogous py-spinnaker2 'experiment runner' partitions and executes single-chip or 48-chip systems, with a Brian2-based software-emulation fallback when no chip is available.

attributes.pipeline_position: sPyNNaker (compile/map, via SpiNNTools partitioning/placement/routing) -> SpiNNaker runtime (this node, data load + SpiN1API execution + readback) -> SpiNNaker 1/2 hardware.

nodes.name: sPyNNaker
nodes.summary: The PyNN backend (pyNN.spiNNaker) plus SpiNNTools execution engine that translates a PyNN network into an application graph, partitions it into a machine graph (~256 atoms/core given per-core SDRAM/DTCM budgets), places/routes it onto SpiNNaker cores (compressing routing tables to the ~1024-entry-per-chip router budget), loads compiled C executables, and extracts results after execution.

nodes.name: Static frames
nodes.summary: Conventional dense RGB/grayscale image input (MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet-scale datasets), the default representation of both the classical/QCFS-lineage ANN-to-SNN conversion literature and any converted-CNN deployment (Akida, Loihi via SNN Toolbox/NxTF).

attributes.usage: The image-classification-static workload is static-frames by definition. Classical and low-latency conversion papers compare Poisson-rate spike trains against direct/analog constant-current first-layer input on exactly this representation; the QCFS lineage and its audited descendants uniformly use direct/analog input. A frame-camera or a frames-from-events reconstruction can equally feed this representation once a dense tensor exists.

nodes.name: Synchronous global tick
nodes.summary: Every core advances the same discrete time index in lockstep, enforced by an explicit barrier handshake (Loihi), a hardware timer interrupt (SpiNNaker), or a single global clock signal (TrueNorth, Tianjic). T is a logical/synchronization unit whose wall-clock duration is not fixed by the timestep count alone.

attributes.platforms_and_meaning_of_T: Loihi 1/2: fixed-size, discrete timesteps synchronized across cores (and, at scale, across the whole mesh) via explicit barrier messages over the asynchronous NoC; a timestep's real-world duration varies with spike traffic and congestion, and the paper stresses these algorithmic timesteps 'need not have a direct relationship to the hardware execution time.' SpiNNaker 1/2: a discrete timer interrupt, standardly 1 ms per timestep to match biological real time; this 1 ms convention is a software/API default, not a hardware limit, and sub-millisecond timesteps (e.g. 0.1 ms) have been used for higher accuracy at the cost of proportionally slower real-time factor. Xylo: a synchronous time-stepped architecture with a global time-step dt (master clock up to 50-100 MHz), genuinely executing one network update per global tick, up to 15 input events/channel and 31 output spikes/neuron processed within each tick. TrueNorth and Tianjic: per NeuroScale (Nature Communications 2025), TrueNorth uses an externally controlled ~1 kHz signal distributed to all hardware components to advance time for every component, and Tianjic uses a global clock for all its coordination processes including advancing time; both, together with Loihi and Loihi 2, advance through a single global barrier with no notion of one layer being ahead of another in tick count.

nodes.name: SyncNN
nodes.summary: FPGA-based (Xilinx ZCU102/ZCU104/ZED, physical boards) rate-encoding IF accelerator that mathematically proves a synchronous reformulation of standard multi-timestep asynchronous IF+reset-by-subtraction execution: only the Poisson input-encoding layer runs for the full T-step window, downstream layers compute the equivalent spike count in one shot via Vm/Vth division.

attributes.time_model: Synchronous, clock-driven FPGA execution; input-layer Poisson encoding still needs the full T-step window, downstream layers run once per inference.
attributes.neuron_models: Explicit IF model.
attributes.reset_semantics: Explicit, native reset-by-subtraction (Vm[o] -= Vth), proven mathematically equivalent to the standard iterative threshold-and-subtract execution.
attributes.payload: Binary spikes; Poisson-rate input encoding.
attributes.weight_precision: 16/8/4-bit configurable.
attributes.operator_coverage: LeNet, Network-in-Network, and VGG architectures evaluated (MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10).
attributes.toolchain: Vitis HLS/SDSoC hardware-mode build.
attributes.availability: Academic FPGA implementation (open-source), not a commercial product.

nodes.name: Tactile sensor
nodes.summary: A touch/e-skin sensor whose output is converted into DVS-like or spike-domain events before reaching a spiking chip: a GelSight optical-tactile front end generating marker-motion events (GelNeuro), or a fiber-Bragg-grating (FBG) e-skin generating touch events (DYNAP-SE tactile localization).

attributes.platforms: GelNeuro (2026): a GelSight optical-tactile front end feeds DVS-like marker-motion events directly into a physical Speck2f DYNAP-CNN spiking CNN, no frame reconstruction; 96.3% accuracy on 15-class texture recognition, 80 ms inference window, 19.6 mW board-level active power, over three orders of magnitude lower than conventional CPU/GPU baselines. DYNAP-SE tactile localization (Ortone et al. 2026): an FBG-based e-skin drives an SNN mimicking early somatosensory processing, implemented on physical DYNAP-SE (4,096 adaptive-exponential analog neurons); 5.33 +/- 0.15 mm localization error (only 8% worse than software), 185 uW median inference power, 8.7 uW resting power.

nodes.name: Mixed Time-step Training
nodes.summary: Stagewise mixed-horizon training produces weights robust across timestep settings. The physical Speck2e route runs fully event-driven and does not execute the training horizon vector as a static chip schedule.

nodes.name: Tsinghua Tianjic
nodes.summary: Many-core, reconfigurable hybrid chip explicitly designed to run both ANNs and SNNs on the same silicon using a shared axon/synapse/dendrite/soma/router abstraction; demonstrated driving an unmanned bicycle performing simultaneous real-time perception and control tasks. Commercial lineage continues via Lynxi's KA200/HP300 products.

attributes.time_model: SNN-mode FCores use spike-event/temporal dynamics with membrane integration, threshold crossing, and reset; ANN-mode FCores instead refresh weighted activations every cycle with no persistent temporal state -- both coexist per-core.
attributes.neuron_models: SNN-mode FCores support spiking neuron dynamics; some FCores can relay full-precision non-spiking membrane potentials between dendritic compartments in "ANN mode", improving large-scale-SNN accuracy by 11.5 percentage points over an SNN-only configuration.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: unknown
attributes.operator_coverage: Reconfigurable axon/synapse/dendrite/soma/router building blocks shared between ANN and SNN modes.
attributes.toolchain: First-generation automatic model-mapping/compiling toolchain (Tsinghua); commercial descendant is Lynxi's BIDL/Lyngor/LynSDK stack.
attributes.availability: Research chip (2019 Nature paper); commercial lineage continues through Lynxi Technologies spinout products.

nodes.name: Sampled time series
nodes.summary: Sampled sequential/time-domain sensor data (audio, surface EMG, scalp EEG, IMU, force-torque, encoder feedback) consumed by directly trained or hardware-in-the-loop-trained SNNs, rather than a static-image ANN converted to spikes.

attributes.usage: Keyword spotting and audio classification: Xylo Audio 2 (95% acc Aloha KWS, 6.6 uJ/inference), Akida (0.72 ms latency, >1,300 keywords/s), Loihi keyword spotter. Biosignal decoding: EMG gesture classification on Loihi (90% acc, 0.37 mJ/inference; 74% acc/5.7 ms/41 mW on Kapoho Bay), EEG seizure prediction on Loihi 2 (99.14% acc, 25.1 mJ/input). Robotics and control: force-torque-driven peg-in-hole insertion on Loihi 1/2, proprioceptive-state-trained mapless navigation (SDDPG) on Loihi. Hardware-in-the-loop training on BrainScaleS-1/2 also operates on time-series-style spike trains injected into the analog substrate.

nodes.name: Tracking and motion estimation
nodes.summary: Optical flow, feature tracking, and motion estimation from vision (usually event-camera) input. Overwhelmingly a GPU/workstation and embedded-CPU/Jetson workload in the surveyed literature; essentially absent from genuine neuromorphic silicon, in contrast to gesture recognition and simple closed-loop robot control.

attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: NOT FOUND on physical spiking silicon in this survey. E-RAFT, RAFT-spline/bflow (dense optical flow, DSEC/MVSEC benchmarks) train and evaluate on CUDA GPUs with no embedded or neuromorphic deployment. rt_of_low_high_res_event_cameras requires a CUDA GPU library, with 'real-time' meaning GPU real-time. IBM's Neuromorphic Optical Flow work (CVPR 2023) explicitly frames the problem as needing model simplification because full-accuracy optical-flow networks are 'prohibitive for application at the edge or in robots,' itself evidence that the default/baseline compute target is a GPU. High-Speed Altitude Regulation with Neuromorphic Camera computes optical flow on a Raspberry Pi 5 (embedded CPU, not a spiking chip). The survey's own rough count places optical flow and tracking outside the small minority of tasks (gesture recognition, simple closed-loop robot control) where genuine spiking/neuromorphic silicon is used at all.

nodes.name: IBM TrueNorth
nodes.summary: Fully digital, event-driven neurosynaptic chip (28 nm, 4096 cores, 1M neurons, 256M synapses, ~65-70 mW) evaluated once per 1 kHz global "tick"; its Eedn training/deployment methodology encodes activation magnitude spatially across redundant trinary-weighted neuron copies within a single tick, not via multi-timestep temporal rate accumulation. Discontinued; superseded conceptually by the non-spiking NorthPole NPU.

attributes.time_model: Global 1 kHz synchronization signal ("tick"); all neurons evaluated once per tick; whole-network evaluation completes within one tick for the Eedn deployment methodology ("one classification per hardware tick").
attributes.neuron_models: Configurable augmented IF model (23 parameters), deterministic/stochastic leak, positive and negative thresholds, reproduces all 20 Izhikevich behavior classes via 1-3 simple neuron instances.
attributes.reset_semantics: Natively configurable: "normal mode" (hard reset to Rj), "linear mode" (reset-by-subtraction, residual potential above threshold retained), and a stochastic non-reset mode -- reset-by-subtraction is first-class hardware-native.
attributes.payload: 1-bit binary spikes only; no native multi-bit/graded payload.
attributes.weight_precision: No native multi-bit weight; trinary weights ({-1,0,+1}) constructed via a pair of neuron copies over a 4-entry axon-type lookup table mapping to signed integers in [-255,255].
attributes.on_chip_learning: None; inference-only, all training (Eedn) happens off-chip.
attributes.operator_coverage: 256 input axons x 256x256 binary synaptic crossbar x 256 neurons per core, time-multiplexed; whole-network mapped across up to 4096 cores/chip.
attributes.toolchain: Eedn (backprop training with trinary weights + triangle-function surrogate) -> Corelet compiler -> NS1e/NS16e boards.
attributes.availability: Not commercially available; discontinued since mid-2010s DARPA SyNAPSE era, distributed only to a limited research ecosystem (30+ institutions).

nodes.name: Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) / latency coding
nodes.summary: Each neuron fires at most once; the timing of that single spike encodes the value. Achieves extreme sparsity but requires long training-time windows for useful spike-time gradients, and firing times must be quantized on real hardware (reintroducing a quantization floor). No soft reset of membrane potentials is needed for TTFS coding since neurons fire at most once.

nodes.name: SynSense Xylo
nodes.summary: Separate SynSense digital SNN inference ASIC family for audio/IMU/low-dimensional sensory signals (XyloAudio 2/3, XyloIMU), genuinely clocked and synchronous (up to 50-100 MHz internal clock, global timestep dt), with native subtractive reset and up to 31 output spikes per neuron per timestep.

attributes.time_model: Synchronous, time-stepped architecture with a global hardware clock/timestep dt (up to 50-100 MHz internal); genuinely one hardware update per dt, unlike the asynchronous Speck/DYNAP-CNN line.
attributes.neuron_models: Current-based LIF (CUBA-LIF) with per-neuron/per-synapse configurable time constants, up to two synaptic states per hidden neuron.
attributes.reset_semantics: Subtractive reset is a fixed hardware property ("Reset during event generation is performed by subtraction"), not a software-switchable option.
attributes.payload: Up to 31 spikes/timestep for hidden neurons, 1 for output neurons -- deviates from the single-spike-per-step assumption of most conversion theory.
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit weights.
attributes.operator_coverage: Up to ~1000 hidden neurons (XyloAudio 2) / 992 (XyloAudio 3) / 496 (XyloIMU); 8-32 output channels; 16 input event channels; ~124-150 KB on-chip memory.
attributes.toolchain: Rockpool (mapper() -> quantize_methods -> config_from_specification()) -> XyloSamna/XyloMonitor.
attributes.availability: Commercially orderable Dev Kits (pricing on application); no research-membership gate.

nodes.name: Rockpool Xylo mapper/quantizer

nodes.name: Xylo simulator (XyloSim)

attributes.toolchain: Rockpool mapper() -> quantize_methods -> config_from_specification() -> XyloSim, the same configuration that XyloSamna sends to the chip.

preserved: classification accuracy of the source quantized CNN (subject to a real accuracy cost at low bit-width without calibration/retraining, e.g. one independent study observed a drop from 90% to 30% before mitigation)
legacy_preserves: classification accuracy of the source quantized CNN (subject to a real accuracy cost at low bit-width without calibration/retraining, e.g. one independent study observed a drop from 90% to 30% before mitigation)
legacy_breaks: BREAKS essentially every primitive the rate-coded conversion literature assumes: no user-exposed multi-timestep simulation horizon T (collapses to a single feedforward pass); no membrane potential carried across timesteps; no reset-by-subtraction (static threshold-once instead of iterative subtract-and-carry); rate coding of an activation as a spike count over T is explicitly replaced by 'squashing the rate-code approximation of the ReLU into one time step', represented as a step-wise quantized ReLU
routes.mechanism: CNN2SNN's convert() writes an Akida .fbz model that the Akida runtime loads for execution on physical AKD1000, AKD1500 or Akida Pico hardware.
routes.notes: Scoped to BrainChip standard converted-CNN execution, as on cnn2snn-to-akida. The physical measurements on this route are recorded on the cnn2snn-to-akida and akida-runtime-to-akida edges.

legacy_breaks: event-domain computation; native asynchronous sparsity
routes.mechanism: The overwhelming majority of published event-vision pipelines accumulate the event-camera stream into a dense frame or voxel-grid buffer over a fixed time window before any neural network sees it.
routes.notes: Documented as the dominant, default approach, not a minority special case; the frame-reconstruction step itself never runs on spiking hardware.

preserved: asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) event stream, unmodified
legacy_preserves: asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) event stream, unmodified
routes.mechanism: An event camera's raw AER output can be consumed directly by an event-driven spiking chip with no frame buffer in between, e.g. Speck's on-die DVS array feeding its co-integrated DYNAP-CNN core.
routes.notes: The minority path relative to frames-from-events.

legacy_breaks: native event-domain sparsity: the DVS->frame accumulation step happens off-chip before conversion, so the deployed pipeline is not end-to-end event-native despite running on physical Loihi
routes.mechanism: The only conversion-based event-vision deployment reaching physical silicon (Massa et al. 2020, Loihi DVS Gesture) first pre-accumulates DVS events into frames off-chip, trains a conventional DNN on those frames, and only then applies classical rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion (SNN Toolbox) before Loihi execution. No paper pairs a genuinely native (non-frame-reconstructed) event stream with rate-coded conversion on physical hardware.
routes.notes: The single E1 exception (Massa et al. 2020) is frame-preprocessed, not native; the broader QCFS/low-latency conversion lineage evaluated on event-vision-adjacent tasks has zero physical-silicon deployments (16/16 audited papers are E5).

preserved: hard-reset (v_reset != None) neuron export, faithfully represented since NIR's spiking primitives only encode fixed-value reset
legacy_preserves: hard-reset (v_reset != None) neuron export, faithfully represented since NIR's spiking primitives only encode fixed-value reset
legacy_breaks: BREAKS reset-by-subtraction entirely, and correctly so given the target format: NIR's own primitive specification (six primitives -- CubaLI, CubaLIF, I, IF, LI, LIF, verified directly against nir/ir/neuron.py) defines reset identically for all three spiking primitives as reset-to-a-fixed-value; no NIR primitive specifies reset by subtraction. SpikingJelly's exporter raises NotImplementedError('NIR does not distinguish soft reset.') whenever v_reset is None -- this is correct behavior given that NIR cannot represent that semantics at all, not an implementation bug in SpikingJelly's exporter
routes.mechanism: to_nir.py's _hard_reset() helper converts a SpikingJelly neuron's reset configuration into NIR's IF/LIF/CubaLIF primitive, which specifies only a fixed-value reset (v <- v_reset if spike else v, v_reset defaulting to 0).
routes.notes: NIR 1.0.8 encodes fixed v_reset. The field was introduced in May 2025, so the 2024 NIR paper cannot establish the current field-level reset contract.

legacy_breaks: doubles the number of compartments (hence neurons/memory) consumed on-chip; NxTF's own authors list built-in soft reset as a desired future hardware feature specifically to remove this cost
routes.mechanism: NxSDK's NxCore register-level API programs Loihi 1 hardware directly; reset-by-subtraction is realized via a two-compartment soft-reset trick (a silent "soma" compartment inhibits the firing compartment by the threshold amount) because Loihi 1's native reset is hard-to-zero.
routes.notes: E1 establishes the physical NxTF route, not soft reset for every workload. Soft reset uses two compartments and doubles compartment allocation.

preserved: detection accuracy of the source ANN
legacy_preserves: detection accuracy of the source ANN
legacy_breaks: rate-coded IF representation: Sigma-Delta conversion uses 16-bit signed graded-spike payloads representing activation deltas, not binary spike counts under reset-by-subtraction, so this is architecturally distinct from QCFS-style rate-coded conversion
routes.mechanism: A YOLOv3-style detector is converted from a conventional ANN into a Sigma-Delta Neural Network using Loihi 2's native graded-spike payloads, and deployed to a physical 16-chip Loihi 2 VPX board.
routes.notes: The only object-detection network found running on physical spiking silicon in the survey; no rate-coded/IF conversion of an object detector has been demonstrated on any physical chip.

routes.notes: E1 establishes a physical run on the single-core FeNN and FeNN-DMA soft processors; the post-implementation frequency, power, and resource figures are synthesis-tool estimates, not board-measured readings, and are reported here as such rather than as a physical power measurement. reports_deployment_evidence is False here (rather than the brief's default True for a route's last edge) because no official AMD/Xilinx or RISC-V vendor documentation source for this toolchain exists in data/source-registry.json; the only available sources are the preprint and peer-reviewed papers themselves. The E1 evidence class and physical route_state above are unaffected; only this specific structural flag is withheld pending an official source, per check-consistency.py's validate_hardware_routes.
routes.measurement_boundary: FeNN: classification latency and energy of a recurrent SNN spoken-digit classifier on the physical single-core FeNN soft processor, reported as significantly faster than a similar model on Loihi and twice as fast as the same model on an embedded GPU while using half the energy. FeNN-DMA: simulation time and effective throughput of a balanced random network (up to 16,000 neurons, 90% sparsity, 1000 1 ms timesteps) on the physical single-core FeNN-DMA SoC, read from on-chip performance counters, plus classification accuracy on Spiking Heidelberg Digits, N-MNIST, and Braille; separately, post-implementation EDA figures (175 MHz single-core / 143 MHz dual-core, 0.53 W, 54,984 LUTs / 47,759 FFs) are Vivado synthesis estimates, not physical power-probe readings.

routes.mechanism: SpiN1API executes the compiled per-core C executable on physical SpiNNaker 1 silicon after SpiNNTools loads data and parameters.

legacy_breaks: built-in sPyNNaker cell types (e.g. IF_curr_exp) use PyNN-conventional hard-reset LIF/IF semantics by default; reset-by-subtraction is achievable only by writing a bespoke C neuron model implementing a custom neuron_model_has_spiked() callback, not a built-in option
routes.mechanism: sPyNNaker, through SpiNNTools, hands the runtime the partitioned machine graph, the placed vertices, the compressed multicast routing tables, the per-core parameter blocks and the compiled C executables that SpiN1API then executes.
routes.notes: The physical measurements on this route are recorded on the spynnaker-to-spinnaker1 and spinnaker-runtime-to-spinnaker1 edges.

legacy_breaks: built-in sPyNNaker cell types (e.g. IF_curr_exp) use PyNN-conventional hard-reset LIF/IF semantics by default; reset-by-subtraction is achievable only by writing a bespoke C neuron model implementing a custom neuron_model_has_spiked() callback, not a built-in option
routes.mechanism: SpiNNTools partitions the application graph into a machine graph (~256 atoms/core given per-core SDRAM/DTCM budgets), places vertices onto cores, generates and compresses multicast routing tables to the ~1024-entry-per-chip router budget, loads per-core parameter blocks and compiled C executables, and signals synchronized execution start.
routes.notes: Earlier DBN-to-SNN conversion result on a single physical SpiNNaker 1 chip (Stromatias/O'Connor lineage): 95.01% MNIST accuracy, 0.3 W, ~20 ms latency, all measured on silicon.

platform_capabilities.contract_requirement: Map a Rockpool graph to the fixed Xylo recurrent SNN core.
platform_capabilities.support_detail: The mapper assigns supported graph nodes to input, hidden recurrent, and output matrices. Unsupported structures or excess dimensions fail mapping.
platform_capabilities.mapper_limits: The device exposes 16 inputs, 1000 hidden neurons, 8 outputs, bounded fan-out, two hidden synaptic states, one output synaptic state, and per-step spike-count limits.
platform_capabilities.precision_constraints: Weights are 8 bit. Synaptic state, membrane state, and threshold are 16 bit. Decay is encoded with four-bit shift parameters.
platform_capabilities.routing_constraints: The global hidden recurrent matrix and input or output projections must satisfy fixed dimensions, fan-out, and alias constraints.
platform_capabilities.host_responsibilities: Rockpool extracts the graph, maps and quantizes it, generates a hardware configuration, connects through samna, selects operating mode, and collects output or power traces.
